denomProfiles/ame-zion/tagline: "The Freedom Church" of Harriet Tubman, Frederick Douglass and Sojourner Truth.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/coreDoctrines/0: Methodist doctrine in the Articles of Religion.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/coreDoctrines/1: Salvation by grace through faith and growth in holiness.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/coreDoctrines/2: Human equality and freedom as implications of the gospel.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/coreDoctrines/3: Infant and adult baptism and the Lord's Supper as sacraments.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/focuses/0: Abolition and the Underground Railroad in the nineteenth century.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/focuses/1: Education through Livingstone College (Salisbury, North Carolina, 1879).
denomProfiles/ame-zion/focuses/3: Missions in West Africa (Liberia, Ghana, Nigeria) and the Caribbean.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/practices/0: Episcopal government with bishops and a quadrennial General Conference.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/practices/1: Methodist worship with Black gospel preaching and music.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/practices/2: Publishing through the Star of Zion newspaper.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/practices/3: Early ordination of women: Julia Foote as deacon (1894) and Mary Small as elder (1898).
denomProfiles/ame-zion/influenced/0/text: Early ordination of women and anti-slavery witness made it a pioneer.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/influenced/1/name: African Methodist churches in West Africa
denomProfiles/ame-zion/influenced/1/text: Missions planted AME Zion conferences in Liberia, Ghana and Nigeria.
denomProfiles/ame-zion/keyFigures/1/role: Early bishop and historian of the church
denomProfiles/ame-zion/keyFigures/2/role: Evangelist and first woman ordained deacon
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/ta: Global connexional Methodism, re-shaped by disaffiliations and 2024 reforms.
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/co: Doctrinal standards: the Articles of Religion, the EUB Confession of Faith, Wesley's Sermons and Notes.
Scripture as primary, illumined by tradition, experience and reason ("Our Theological Task", 1972).
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as sacraments, with an open table.
Social Principles (1972) setting out positions on society and ethics.
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/fo: Mission and relief through the United Methodist Committee on Relief (UMCOR).
Education: many universities, seminaries and schools.
A worldwide church with rapid growth in Africa and the Philippines.
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/pr: General Conference, Council of Bishops and Judicial Council governing the connexion.
Clergy appointed by bishops to local churches.
Book of Discipline and the United Methodist Hymnal and Book of Worship.
Women given full clergy rights in 1956; Marjorie Matthews was the first woman bishop (1980).
In 2024 General Conference removed bans on gay clergy and same-sex weddings and approved regionalisation.
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/in: Launched in 2022 by traditionalists; many disaffiliating congregations joined it.
American Methodist missions helped plant Korean Methodism from 1885.
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/ke: Co-founder of the United Brethren in Christ (1800)
denomProfiles/united-methodist-church/in: The Methodist Church in India, which grew from the Methodist Episcopal mission begun at Bareilly in 1856, became autonomous in 1981 and remains an affiliated autonomous church of the UMC.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/tagl: Holiness Methodists who stood for free pews, abolition and simple worship.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/core: Salvation by grace through faith offered to all.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as sacraments.
Articles of Religion adapted from Methodism.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/focu: Ministry to the poor: "free" pews open to all instead of rented pews.
Opposition to slavery and to secret oath-bound societies, from its founding.
World mission; most members today live outside North America.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/prac: General Conference with bishops and annual conferences.
Lay delegates with an equal voice to clergy in conference.
Infant and believer's baptism both accepted.
Women ordained as elders since 1974, after earlier evangelist and deacon roles.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/infl: Founded Roberts Wesleyan, Seattle Pacific, Greenville and Spring Arbor universities.
Founded in India by Free Methodist missionary Frank Kline in 1938.
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/keyF: Revivalist whose preaching shaped the early movement
denomProfiles/free-methodist-church/inIn: Free Methodist missionaries worked in the Yavatmal (Yeotmal) district of Maharashtra, where Frank Kline founded Union Biblical Seminary in 1938 (moved to Pune in 1983); there are Free Methodist churches in Maharashtra and other states.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/tagline: Abolitionist and holiness Methodists united in 1968; pioneers in women's ministry.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/coreDoctri: Entire sanctification as a work of grace after conversion.
Salvation by grace through faith offered to all.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as sacraments.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/focuses/1: Social justice, rooted in its abolitionist founding (1843).
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/focuses/2: Church multiplication in North America and abroad.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/focuses/3: Higher education through Indiana Wesleyan, Houghton and other universities.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/practices/: General Conference with general superintendents and districts.
Women ordained since the nineteenth century.
Infant and believer's baptism both accepted.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/influenced: The 1848 Seneca Falls Convention met in a Wesleyan Methodist chapel.
Luther Lee preached at Antoinette Brown's 1853 ordination, the first of a woman in a US denomination.
denomProfiles/wesleyan-church/keyFigures: Abolitionist founder of the Wesleyan Methodist Connection
Abolitionist and advocate of women's preaching
Founder of the International Holiness Union and Prayer League (1897)
Co-founder of the Pilgrim Holiness tradition
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/tag: The largest Wesleyan-Holiness denomination, now present in more than 160 countries and areas.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/cor: Entire sanctification as a second work of grace, cleansing the heart and filling it with love.
Sixteen Articles of Faith in the Manual.
Salvation by grace through faith, available to all.
Scripture inerrant in all things relating to salvation.
Baptism (infant or believer) and the Lord's Supper as sacraments.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/foc: Global mission; most members now live outside the US.
Education through Nazarene universities and seminaries.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/pra: General Assembly, general superintendents, districts and local churches.
The Covenant of Christian Character and Covenant of Christian Conduct for members.
Altar calls and testimony in revivalist worship.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/inf: H. Orton Wiley's Christian Theology (1940-43) became a standard text.
Nazarene missions planted churches in Asia, Africa and Latin America.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/key: Founder of the Los Angeles Church of the Nazarene (1895)
Holiness preacher in the southern founding body
denomProfiles/church-of-the-nazarene/inI: Nazarene mission work in India centres on the Buldhana and Washim districts of Maharashtra, where Reynolds Memorial Hospital at Washim is its best-known institution; churches have since spread to other states.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/tag: Holiness "reformation movement" seeking the visible unity of all believers without denominational walls.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/cor: Entire sanctification as a second work of grace, in the Wesleyan-Holiness tradition.
The church is the whole body of the saved; God alone "sets members" in it, so there is no formal membership roll.
Opposition to sectarianism and creeds as divisive human additions to Scripture.
Divine healing as part of Christ's provision, without rejecting medicine.
Amillennial, non-dispensational reading of the last things.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/foc: Evangelism and publishing through the Gospel Trumpet (later Warner Press).
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/pra: Three ordinances: believer's baptism by immersion, the Lord's Supper and foot-washing.
Open fellowship rather than formal church membership.
Camp meetings, historically centred on Anderson, Indiana.
Women preachers from the movement's earliest decades.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/inf: The movement's radio ministry (from 1947) carried its unity message widely.
It became a partner in the Wesleyan Holiness Connection and in wider unity dialogues.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/key: Founder; editor of the Gospel Trumpet from 1881.
Early theologian of the movement's church-historical prophecy scheme.
Editor and historian who reshaped its self-understanding in the twentieth century.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-anderson/inI: Work in India began in the 1890s through contacts in Calcutta; the Church of God (Anderson) today has congregations notably in Kerala and in Meghalaya, among the Khasi.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/ta: Autonomous Korean Methodism, born of two American missions and united in 1930.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/co: Wesleyan Arminian teaching: prevenient grace, justification by faith and the call to holiness.
Assurance of salvation through the witness of the Spirit.
The 1930 Korean Methodist Doctrinal Statement (Korean Creed), a short confession framed at union.
Two sacraments, baptism and the Lord's Supper.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/fo: Evangelism and church planting in Korea and overseas.
Education, through schools such as Pai Chai and Ewha founded by early missionaries.
Prayer, including the early-morning prayer meetings typical of Korean Protestantism.
Social and national concerns, including Methodist involvement in the 1919 independence movement.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/pr: Episcopal Methodist polity with bishops elected for fixed terms and an annual conference system.
Dawn prayer services and revival meetings.
Ordination of women, practised since the 1950s.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/in: Korean Methodist congregations and missionaries now serve in many countries.
Methodism was one of the two leading Protestant streams, with Presbyterianism, in Korea's twentieth-century church growth.
denomProfiles/korean-methodist-church/ke: Pioneer American Methodist missionary (1885), founder of Pai Chai school.
First general superintendent of the united church (1930).
denomProfiles/evangelical/tagline: Trans-denominational Protestant movement of conversion, the Bible, the cross and activism.
denomProfiles/evangelical/coreDoctrines/: Conversionism: the need for personal faith and new birth.
Biblicism: the Bible as the supreme, trustworthy authority.
Crucicentrism: the atoning death of Christ at the centre of the gospel.
Activism: the gospel expressed in mission and service (Bebbington's four marks).
Salvation by grace through faith, in continuity with the Reformation.
denomProfiles/evangelical/focuses/1: Personal devotion: Bible reading and prayer.
denomProfiles/evangelical/focuses/3: Social reform, from abolition to relief and development work.
denomProfiles/evangelical/practices/0: Preaching-centred worship, increasingly with contemporary music.
denomProfiles/evangelical/practices/1: Parachurch agencies, mission societies and student movements.
denomProfiles/evangelical/practices/3: Cooperation through bodies such as the World Evangelical Alliance and the Lausanne Movement.
denomProfiles/evangelical/influenced/0/t: Pentecostalism emerged from evangelical Holiness circles.
denomProfiles/evangelical/influenced/1/t: Defined a global evangelical consensus on mission.
denomProfiles/evangelical/influenced/2/t: Grew largely within evangelical dispensational circles.
denomProfiles/evangelical/influenced/3/t: Evangelical missions planted many of today's fastest-growing churches.
denomProfiles/evangelical/keyFigures/3/r: Mass evangelist of the twentieth century.
denomProfiles/evangelical/keyFigures/4/r: Anglican leader and chief architect of the Lausanne Covenant.
denomProfiles/evangelical/members/note: Pew Research Center (2011) estimate of evangelical Christians worldwide; definitions vary widely.
denomProfiles/evangelical/inIndia: Evangelical churches and agencies are found across India, coordinated since 1951 by the Evangelical Fellowship of India; they are especially strong in the north-east and the south.
